source: Opus, 2026-11-28, read from the full ORV ch1 (prologue) block dump; SILVER (not owner-verified)
block_indexing: 0-based block index within the chapter, as stored in chapter.blocks_json

scenes.time_relation: the day before the world changes (block 54 says so); the place is not stated: he is reading on his old smartphone
scenes.place: unstated; the panels should centre on the phone screen and the reader's face, with no invented landmark
present: Kim Dokja, the first-person narrator, named only through his comment ID at block 14. His look must come from the whole-novel dossier, because ch1 never describes him.
referenced_only: tls123, the author: present only as on-screen messages. Never draw a face or body; the author's identity is withheld across the whole novel.
the anonymous commenters (text on screen only)
the school delinquents, the university and the military unit (the memory montage)

sub_layers.why: an epigraph quoted from the in-world novel, used as a title card
his life alongside the novel: bullied, a third-rate university, the frontline draft, a contract job

beats: title card or cold open with the epigraph lettered as a poem or card on black (blocks 1-2)
a close-up of the phone screen showing the 'complete' mark (blocks 3-8)
his comment typed to the author (block 14)
the chapter statistics: the numbers on screen, the hit counts falling to 1, as an insert (blocks 16-20)
the recommendation backfires: hostile comments on screen; he goes red-faced (blocks 22-30)
an unexpected message from tls123: a chat exchange rendered as a phone UI (blocks 31-50)
the author logs off; small jealousy (blocks 51-52)
closing narration over an ominous, held image of the ordinary world: a foreshadowing beat (blocks 53-54). No apocalypse imagery, because the text does not show it yet.
scenes.creative_licence: Whole-novel knowledge lets the director make the final caption a dread beat and keep tls123 faceless. It must not depict any later event.

letter_requirements: on-screen text, chat messages and comments rendered as a phone UI, not as speech balloons. This needs a screen/system letter kind, which we do not have yet (a gap that director v2 must close; system windows recur in ORV)
poem or card lettering for the epigraph
narration captions for the first-person voice
speech for the few spoken lines (blocks 4, 12, 29, 52)
